title: Reading Between the Headlines
text:
Headlines are engineered to capture attention before a reader has had any chance to weigh the evidence. A well-chosen adjective or a carefully placed verb can frame an event as a scandal, a triumph, or a tragedy without a single claim being technically false. Discourse analysts therefore examine not only what a story says but also what it presupposes and what it deliberately leaves unsaid.

Critical readers, by contrast, tend to interrogate the source before accepting the narrative. They ask who benefits from a particular framing, whether the statistics have been stripped of their context, and whether competing interpretations have been dismissed too quickly. Such scepticism is not cynicism; it is simply the habit of treating every persuasive text as a construction rather than a window onto reality.

questions.text: According to the first paragraph, what can a carefully placed verb do?
options: Make an event sound like a scandal, triumph, or tragedy
Prove that a statistic is false
Remove all emotion from a story

questions.text: According to the second paragraph, what do critical readers ask about statistics?
options: Whether they were published in a famous journal
Whether they have been stripped of their context
Whether they were calculated by hand
Whether they are written in simple language

questions.text: What does the author imply about persuasive texts?
options: They should be avoided by all readers
They are constructions that deserve careful scrutiny
They are harmless when written by experts

questions.text: How does the author distinguish scepticism from cynicism?
options: Scepticism rejects all evidence, while cynicism accepts it
Scepticism is a habit of careful questioning, while cynicism assumes bad faith
They are two words for the same attitude
Cynicism is a method that discourse analysts require

vocabulary.definition: deliberately designed or arranged to produce a particular result
assumes something to be true before it is stated
a habit of questioning claims before accepting them
to question someone or something closely and thoroughly

paragraph_translations: Manşetler, okuyucunun kanıtları tartma fırsatı bulamadan dikkati çekmek için tasarlanır. Yerinde seçilmiş bir sıfat ya da özenle yerleştirilmiş bir fiil, tek bir iddia teknik olarak yanlış olmadan bir olayı skandal, zafer ya da trajedi gibi gösterebilir. Söylem analistleri bu yüzden yalnızca bir haberin ne söylediğini değil, neyi önceden varsaydığını ve neyi bilerek söylemediğini de inceler.

Eleştirel okuyucular ise tersine, hikâyeyi kabul etmeden önce kaynağı sorgulama eğilimindedir. Bir çerçevelemenin kimin yararına olduğunu, istatistiklerin bağlamından koparılıp koparılmadığını ve rakip yorumların çok hızlı reddedilip reddedilmediğini sorarlar. Bu şüphecilik bir kinizm değildir; her ikna edici metni gerçekliğe açılan bir pencere değil, bir yapı olarak ele alma alışkanlığıdır.
